outcomeNote: A single amoraic restriction of the mishna's case; no challenge in this unit.

segments.he: הַתּוֹקֵעַ לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִים עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר, אֲבָל אוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִין בַּבּוֹר — יָצְאוּ.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna: If «one sounds» a shofar «into a pit or into a cistern,» he has not fulfilled his obligation. «Rav Huna said: They taught» this «only with respect to those standing at the edge of the pit,» i.e., on the outside, as they can hear only the echo coming from the pit. «But those standing in the pit» itself «have fulfilled their obligation,» since they initially hear the sound of the shofar.

the mishna's ruling that one who hears an echo has not fulfilled his obligation applies only to those standing at the edge of the pit, not to those inside it

positions.claim: only those standing at the edge of the pit fail to fulfill their obligation; those inside the pit have fulfilled it
positions.basis: those inside hear the shofar's own sound, not an echo
